LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 SEQUENCING IDEAS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we sequence ideas in paragraphs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify main parts of a composition for expression
2. write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 3.3.1 SEQUENCING IDEAS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 3.3.1 SEQUENCING IDEAS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify main parts of a composition for expression

What this means
In this part you learn to identify main parts of a composition for expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify main parts of a composition for expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify main parts of a composition for expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify main parts of a composition for expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas to a partner. (skill: write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify main parts of a composition for expression.
3. Practise this skill: write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we sequence ideas in paragraphs?
2. How can we prevent some disasters in the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify main parts of a composition for expression.
5. Be able to: write a composition in a logical sequence for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
